subject.title: [security] GET portal logout allows cross-site session termination

question: Should Crabbox change portal logout from a cross-site navigable GET into a same-origin state-changing action, and what compatibility shape should that take?
rationale: The vulnerability is source-backed, but the permanent fix changes a browser auth/session boundary and may affect existing portal logout links or cookie behavior.

options.title: Require same-origin logout intent
options.body: Convert logout to POST or add an explicit same-origin CSRF/intent token, apply the gate before revocation and cookie clearing, and cover both blocked and allowed flows in Worker tests.

options.title: Tighten cookie behavior only
options.body: Changing crabbox_session to SameSite=Strict may reduce cross-site navigation exposure but needs login-flow compatibility proof and leaves a state-changing GET design in place.

options.title: Document GET logout as intentional
options.body: Maintainers can accept forced logout as a low-availability tradeoff, but that would need explicit documentation because it conflicts with the current portal mutation boundary.

recommendation.title: Require same-origin logout intent
recommendation.body: Convert logout to POST or add an explicit same-origin CSRF/intent token, apply the gate before revocation and cookie clearing, and cover both blocked and allowed flows in Worker tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on logout revocation and adjacent portal security makes this the strongest available routing signal.
